issues.issue: The Licensee is identified only as "you", with no named person or entity in the operative granting sentence, so who is bound (Garrett Salpeter personally or ARPwave Austin LLC, his employer on the form above) is genuinely open. "the ARP POV System, described above" also points to a form that describes only quantity and price, not a system.

The heading and grant call this a "BRONZE SYSTEM LICENSE" of "the ARP POV System", while section 1.1 defines System(s) as all intellectual property and equipment associated with ARP Wave LLC and section 1.2 limits the license to five enumerated items; the three descriptions of the licensed subject matter do not line up.

"all other intellectual property and equipment associated with ARP Wave LLC" has no discernible boundary — "associated with" could reach every protocol, program and device the Licensor owns — and the enumerated "proprietary protocols and programs" sit against that open-ended catch-all. "Used commercially" is likewise undefined for a licensee whose stated business is operating an ARPwave clinic.

"This agreement is non-cancellable for any reason" cannot be squared with section 7.1 (revocation "if this Agreement is terminated"), 7.2 ("Upon termination of this Agreement for any reason") and 7.3 (survival after termination), all of which presuppose that the Agreement can be terminated.

The license is granted for the ARP POV SYSTEM "which consists of the following" five items, an exhaustive enumeration inviting an expressio unius reading, yet items such as "DISCOUNTS ON CUSTOM TRAINING PROGRAMS AND PROTOCOLS" state no discount and no term.

The closed five-item list conflicts with the far broader definition of "System(s)" in section 1.1 (all protocols, programs, intellectual property and equipment associated with ARP Wave LLC), leaving it unclear which body of material the licence, confidentiality (3.2) and return (7.2) obligations attach to.

The clause sets a 60-month "original term" but then lets the Licensee keep the System(s) indefinitely afterwards "at no additional charge" except for unspecified "charges applicable for time use" at rates "set forth on page one", which the attached form does not set out.

A definite 60-month term with a "License End Date" is hard to reconcile with section 1.1's statement that the agreement "is non-cancellable for any reason" and with sections 7.1-7.3, which contemplate termination and post-termination return of the System(s).
The rights are said to be "forfeitable in the event of certain circumstances or occurrences as herein set forth", but the phrase names no circumstance and points nowhere identifiable.
The cross-reference to forfeiture events "as herein set forth" has no referent: Section 5 (Default) never defines an event of default, and no other provision enumerates forfeiture triggers.
Section 1.5 bars enhancements without consent, while section 7.2 requires return of "enhancements" on termination, implying they may exist; the tension is minor and readily harmonised.
"Misuse or negligence on the part of Licensee" is the sole allocator of repair cost and is left wholly undefined, and "defects" is not distinguished from ordinary wear.

Free repair is promised only "during the original term", which sits awkwardly with section 1.3's provision that the Licensee may keep the unit indefinitely after the original term at no additional charge.

The duty to "keep the ARP POV Unit in good repair" overlaps with section 2.1's promise of free Licensor repair during the original term, but the two are reconcilable through the misuse/negligence carve-out.

"Full replacement value thereof as determined by the Licensor" leaves the insured amount to one party's unilateral determination while also fixing it at $7560.00, and the required "liability and property damage insurance" has no stated limit.
The stated replacement value of $7560.00 does not match the "Total Cost Of Plans: $7500" recorded on the face of the same instrument.

"The Protocols licensed in conjunction with the System(s)" is capitalised as if defined but is never defined, and "acting outside the scope of use" gives no ascertainable boundary for the conduct required.

The confidentiality duty attaches to "all System(s)", which under section 1.1 includes physical equipment, and there is no carve-out for information already public or independently known, so the reach of the secrecy obligation is genuinely uncertain.

A duty to keep the System(s) "strictly confidential" and not to "display" them is hard to reconcile with the licensed use contemplated by section 1.2 (applying the unit to an "applicatee" under section 3.1), and with section 1.3's continuing possession right.

The disclaimer excludes "warranties of marketability" rather than merchantability, a mechanical error that may defeat the disclaimer of the implied warranty of merchantability, which by statute must be mentioned by name.

The first sentence preserves claims for "breach or breaches of Licensor's contractual obligations herein set forth" while the second waives "all rights at law and equity" to claim fraud, imperfection or "any form of redress with respect to said System(s)", so the scope of what survives the waiver is internally uncertain.

The blanket waiver of fraud claims sits against section 5.2 and Section 4's other disclaimers, and against the Licensor's affirmative repair obligation in section 2.1, which the waiver would render unenforceable.

The clause opens "Notwithstanding any said repossession" although no repossession right has been stated anywhere, and it waives damages on "the occurrence of an event of default under this section" though Section 5 never defines an event of default.

Section 5 contains no enumerated events of default and no repossession remedy, so this clause's cross-references to "said repossession" and "an event of default under this section" cannot be squared with the instrument read as a whole (cf. section 1.4, which also assumes forfeiture events "as herein set forth").
Fees are recoverable for enforcement "under this License Agreement or any related agreements", and "related agreements" is nowhere defined or identified.
The reference to "any related agreements" is in tension with section 7.7, which declares this License to be the entire agreement between the parties.

"Any other agreement signed contemporaneously between Licensor and Licensee" identifies no agreement and fixes no window for "contemporaneously", and "any default" is untethered to any defined event of default.
Importing defaults from other contemporaneous agreements cannot be reconciled with section 7.7's integration clause making this License "the entire agreement between the parties hereto".

"Shall be sent facsimile transmission-or overnight courier" omits the preposition and, more importantly, the clause gives a notice address only for the Licensor, leaving notice to the Licensee unprovided for.
The Licensor's address here (Apple Valley, MN 55337) contradicts the address given in the opening grant clause (7721 145th West, Apple Valley MN 55124).

The operative middle of the clause is unreadable garbled text, so the trigger and scope of the automatic revocation and reassignment of "any rights herein set forth" cannot be determined from the words used.

Revocation "if this Agreement is terminated" presupposes a right of termination that section 1.1 denies ("non-cancellable for any reason"), and no termination mechanism appears anywhere in the instrument.
"Renditions or enhancements of all System(s)" is undefined and, given the section 1.1 definition covering all ARP Wave intellectual property, the extent of what must be returned is uncertain.

Immediate return on termination "for any reason" is difficult to reconcile with section 1.3, which permits the Licensee to retain the System(s) after the original term, and with section 1.1's "non-cancellable" statement.

Survival after termination presupposes a termination right that section 1.1 forecloses by declaring the agreement "non-cancellable for any reason", though the clause is easily harmonised as contingent.
The clause requires strict compliance with "the ARP Unit Manual" and its "Cautionary and Warning language", neither of which is defined, attached or otherwise identified in the instrument.
It duplicates the protocol-compliance duty in section 3.1 but adds the Manual as a second, unincorporated standard, leaving which document controls unresolved.

Section 7.6 permits assignment of the Licensor's rights "without notice", while section 7.8 separately governs assignment of the Agreement; the two overlapping assignment clauses use different language but do not squarely conflict.

The integration clause declaring this License "the entire agreement" conflicts with section 5.2, which makes a default under "any other agreement signed contemporaneously" a default here, and with sections 5.2 and 7.9's references to "related agreements".

Section 7.8's bar on Licensee assignment restates section 1.4, and its grant of Licensor assignment rights duplicates section 7.6 (which dispenses even with notice); the overlap invites but does not compel an argument about which controls.

"All actions or proceedings relating to this Agreement or any related agreements" leaves both the reach of "relating to" (tort, trade-secret and non-party claims) and the undefined phrase "any related agreements" open, and the clause mixes consent to jurisdiction with a mandatory "must be litigated" venue command.

The forum clause binds "each party", but the instrument never names the Licensee other than as "you" in the opening grant, so whether it binds the individual signatory or his company must be resolved from elsewhere in the document.
The judicial-reformation sentence directs that an overbroad provision "shall be sufficiently narrowed so as to make it enforceable" without any standard for how far to narrow it.
